title: Same seed,
subtitle: same game.
summary: A fixed step, a seeded random and state in typed arrays: runs replay, peers stay in lockstep, and syncCheck proves it.
lead: A Fizlet sim that steps on a fixed `dt`, draws every random number from `engine.random` and keeps its state in typed arrays replays exactly from a seed. That is what makes a replay test possible, and what lets two players run the same game in lockstep with only their inputs crossing the wire.

blocks.heading: The rules for a deterministic step

items: **Seeded random only.** `engine.random()` is seeded by `createEngine({ seed })` and allocation-free; `engine.random.state` snapshots and restores it. No `Math.random` in the step.
**No clock in the step.** Use `dt` and `engine.steps` (an integer count of fixed steps), never `performance.now()` or `Date`.
**No layout reads.** A sim that reads the page depends on the screen. In net play, fix the arena size and scale the drawing.
**Inputs as bits.** Pack what a player does into one 32-bit word per frame; the step reads only the words.
**Nothing else moves on engine steps.** Anything that advances with the step (a drop timer, a random draw in an effect) must advance on the same frames on every peer.

blocks.heading: `syncCheck`: find the first frame that differs

body.text: `syncCheck(setup, { players, frames, latency, jitter })` from `@fzlt/core/presence/check` runs your sim as lockstep clients over an in-memory link with the latency and jitter you ask for, hashes each client's state every frame and returns `{ ok, frames, diverged, stalls }`. `diverged` is the first frame whose state differed, or -1. It is test-only code ({size:@fzlt/core/presence/check} gzip) and never ships to players.

The presence brick's own tests run two clients byte-identical for 3,000 frames with no latency, stay identical with delayed, jittered and reordered inputs at unequal frame rates, run four players at latency 3, and catch a forced desync at the next hash check.

seo.title: Deterministic games in Fizlet: seeds and lockstep
seo.description: Make a Fizlet sim replay from a seed: fixed step, seeded random, typed arrays and input bits. syncCheck finds the first frame where two peers differ.
